title: Microsoft Teams: admin list of custom apps that need updates for private and shared channels
summary: Hold: the manifest-only update guidance omits Microsoft's conditions about team membership and cross-team data, so administrators could request insufficient updates. The roadmap facts, Message Center dates, admin paths and PowerShell call are supported; licensing needs a narrower explanation.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin switch specifically for the compatibility list.

claims.claim: How the admin list determines incompatibility, including reliance on supportsChannelFeatures, is not documented.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: In app manifest v1.25 and later, supportsChannelFeatures replaces supportedChannelTypes.
claims.quote: Replace supportedChannelTypes with supportsChannelFeatures when you update your app manifest to v1.25 or later.

claims.claim: An app with no dependence on channel membership, files, cross-channel data or user type needs only supportsChannelFeatures: tier1 added and testing.
claims.quote: Use channel or team membership to determine message delivery, task assignment, or permissions; Access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint; Combine or share data across multiple channels or teams; Customize experience, based on users (internal, guests, or external members)
claims.fix: Replace the clause with: 'An app that does not use channel or team membership to determine message delivery, task assignment or permissions, access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint, combine or share data across multiple channels or teams, or customize the experience based on internal, guest or external users needs only supportsChannelFeatures: tier1 added to its manifest and verification and testing across channels.' This preserves the full conditions at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/platform/build-apps-for-shared-private-channels#enable-apps-for-shared-and-private-channels.

claims.claim: Apps already published with an earlier manifest version continue to work.
claims.quote: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.

claims.claim: A manifest declaring supportedChannelTypes cannot be uploaded or submitted under v1.25 and later.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use supportsChannelFeatures instead of supportedChannelTypes. If your app manifest declares supportedChannelTypes, you can't upload or submit your app.

claims.claim: Message extension-only apps operating exclusively in personal scope do not require updates for availability in shared and private channels.
claims.quote: Message extension–only apps that operate exclusively in personal scope do not require updates to be available for users in Shared and Private channels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Private and shared channels have their own SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Unlike standard channels, which share a SharePoint site with the team, private and shared channels have their own SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that failure to account for channel membership, storage or privacy can cause unintended data exposure.
claims.quote: Ensure that you understand how different channels determine app functionality, membership, storage, or privacy. Otherwise, you might encounter broken functionality or unintended data exposure:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Channel members can include guests and cross-tenant users.
claims.quote: Channel members might include in-tenant users, guests, or cross-tenant users (external users from other tenants).

claims.claim: Apps that distinguish users for access, data visibility or features must validate roles and tenant IDs.
claims.quote: If your app needs to distinguish between various users to manage access, data visibility, and feature availability, then you must validate user roles and tenant IDs before granting permissions.

claims.claim: Custom apps are built within or commissioned for the organisation.
claims.quote: Your organization can commission the creation of custom apps for your org-specific requirements. Custom apps can be developed within your organization or by app developers outside the organization.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings to sources for the statement about who builds custom apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft will not update custom apps.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams custom apps built organization developer update apps line of business. Read Manage apps support section and Manage custom apps update section; they say developers publish updates, not that Microsoft never updates custom apps.
claims.fix: Remove 'so Microsoft will not update them'; retain the developer responsibility supported by MC1459131.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific licensing is published, so the page shows licensing as unknown.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access to sources and replace the licensing explanation with: 'Teams requires a Teams license for each organisational user except for anonymously joining meetings. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to this admin list.' Retain the Teams Administrator role statement and narrow Open questions and the cost rationale to feature-specific licensing.
